stories.title: Pip and the Book That Could Wait
stories.outro: See you next time in Sunny Meadow!
stories.moral: A break can help you return to something you enjoy.
moralRhyme: Mark your place and rest today,
Your book can wait while you go play!

youtube.title: Pip and the Book That Could Wait | Sunny Meadow
youtube.description: Pip read the same little page for the third time. Bao watched his friend's eyelids droop above the book. A gentle friendship story. A break can help you return to something you enjoy. #SunnyMeadow #DreamyDiscoveries

lines.text: Pip read the same little page for the third time.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Bao watched his friend's eyelids droop above the book.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I like this story, but the words keep slipping away.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You have been looking at it for a long while.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip wanted to finish before putting the book down.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Its painted forest had seemed exciting at first.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I promised myself I would reach the final page today.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Does that promise leave any room for a little rest?
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip tried reading the page much faster.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The pictures passed before he noticed their small details.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now I have reached farther, but I missed that part.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You can turn back. There is no race inside the cover.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip tried sitting very straight to make himself concentrate.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He opened his eyes as wide as he could.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Perhaps my sleepy eyes just need a stronger command.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Your eyes seem to be asking for a break instead.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Does Pip have to finish the whole book now?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Pip closed the book without marking his place.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then he opened it and could not find the forest page.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now taking a break has made another problem!
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: We could find your page and leave a marker there.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip looked through the pictures at a gentle pace.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He found the painted tree where his reading had stopped.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Here it is. I remember that very curly branch.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: A marker can keep that place while your eyes rest.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Bao offered a plain strip of clean spare paper.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Pip placed it between the forest page and the next.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: This little strip can hold my place for me.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And you can close the book without losing your tree.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip shut the cover around his new paper bookmark.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: His wings felt lighter without the heavy open pages.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I thought stopping meant giving up on the whole story.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You can want to return and still rest right now.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: They stepped outside to the quiet garden path.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Pip stretched his wings while Bao looked at the flowers.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Real trees have very curly branches too.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And they stay here when we go back indoors.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: What can save the place for later?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Pip enjoyed a short walk instead of rushing to finish.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The story waited where he had left it on the table.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I am beginning to wonder about the next picture again.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: We can head back when you want another look.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip chose to return after watching a small leaf fall.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: His paper marker stuck out from the waiting book.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: My little strip has done an excellent keeping job.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: It has stayed on the tree page all afternoon.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip read the forest page slowly enough to notice it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He spotted a tiny painted bridge beside the roots.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I missed that bridge when I hurried before.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Your rested eyes have found a new piece of the story.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip reached another page and decided to stop there.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He moved the paper marker before closing the cover.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I still have some story left for tomorrow.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Then tomorrow already has something you want to visit.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Pip gave the plain paper bookmark a friendly little bow.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Bao admired its very important position inside the book.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Thank you for reading absolutely nothing while I rested.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: A perfect job for someone with no eyes at all.
lines.speaker: friend
